translations.translatedText: # Friday 1.1.2021 (radio)
New Year's Day. Fireworks. The President's speech. Changes in 2021.
## Celebrating the New Year
![A firework explodes above a church.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11721740)
Open image viewer
Fireworks were set off at the Senate Square in Helsinki when the year changed. Photo: Esa Syväkuru / Yle
Finns have celebrated the New Year quite quietly. The police say that people followed the corona restrictions to different degrees, however.

In the Turku area the police received reports of several parties with dozens of young people. In Oulu and Rovaniemi too, the police stopped parties with up to 200-300 young people. The police say that in Helsinki, on the other hand, the gathering restrictions were followed quite well.

The fire service put out some fires on New Year's night. In Maaninka in Kuopio there was a building fire in which one person died. In addition, there have been fires at least in Tuusula, Kemijärvi and Muonio.
## Eye injuries from fireworks
![Fireworks shop at the Tokmanni store in Ruoholahti, Helsinki, on 27 December 2020.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11719440)
Open image viewer
Fireworks may only be fired with safety glasses on. Photo: Emmi Korhonen / Lehtikuva
Eye injuries caused by New Year's fireworks have been treated in hospitals.
The university hospitals say that they have treated 7 patients who got eye injuries from fireworks. There have been patients at least in Helsinki, Turku and Kuopio.
The police also received some alarms about fireworks. For example, they set rubbish bins and postboxes on fire. Some people also fired rockets along the ground towards other people.
## The President's New Year speech
![Sauli Niinistö giving a New Year speech behind a desk.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11721406)
Open image viewer
President Sauli Niinistö. Photo: Jon Norppa / Office of the President of the Republic
President Sauli Niinistö has given the traditional New Year's speech.

In the speech President Niinistö said that Finland has so far come through the coronavirus pandemic quite well. The President thanked all Finns for this, but especially health care professionals. The President also said that the corona crisis is not over yet. Because of that, people still need to find strength to follow the restrictions and instructions.
Niinistö also talked about many other things, such as Finland's security, cyber attacks and climate change.
## The year 2021 brings changes
![Bottles of wine on a shelf in the Alko store in Tesoma](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_4032,h_2268,x_0,y_208/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-5760485d2312a501730/1562579641)
Open image viewer
Alcohol is becoming more expensive. Photo: Antti Eintola / Yle
The turn of the year changes many things.

For example, taxation of employees gets a little tougher and the interest deduction on housing loans becomes smaller. Alcohol and tobacco become more expensive. The prices of passports and ID cards will rise.

The age of compulsory education rises to 18 years this year. A young person under 18 must therefore apply for upper secondary education after comprehensive school. Upper secondary education, such as upper secondary school or vocational school, becomes free of charge.
